structured_output.world_model: W2 (empirical), after E048. The tip is E036 at 5.314 s and 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. Identical-code rebuilds (E038, E043, E047) show about 0.3 pp of 3-seed noise and about ±0.03 s of time noise. The population mean is about 0.752. Measured regularities: the epoch dial costs about 1.5-2 s/pp. Backward truncation is the best lever. Early 20 px is nearly free. Time-neutral boosters mostly fail. Anything that changes the math or the RNG reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. For the three systems and architecture ideas here, I expect I079 to cost a little time (max-autotune-no-cudagraphs is likely slower, roughly +1-3%). I expect I080 to save time (the 31x31 conv plus pool becomes a stride-2 conv, which is about 2x cheaper there) and to lose some accuracy (the pool is replaced by a strided conv and the stem changes). I081 is a stack of near-misses and is likely to come out near the tip in time. I082 is a deeper group-2 freeze, with a small time gain.

forecasts.reason: No-cudagraph autotune probably costs a bit; determinism across builds is plausible but a commit needs <=0.5% time cost, which is unlikely.
Removes the biggest memory-bound stem tensor, so time falls, but the stride-conv swap changes the features and likely costs 0.1-0.3 pp.
Selection and top-up roughly cancel on the dial's line, so the result lands near the tip within noise.
A deeper group-2 freeze saves a bit more time per E046, and the accuracy cost is within noise, with a cliff risk as in E037.

cruxes: Is build-to-build kernel reselection the source of the 0.3 pp 3-seed spread, and can it be pinned cheaply?
Does a strided 3x3 conv replacing conv+maxpool at the stem keep accuracy within 0.15 pp while cutting 31x31 memory traffic?
Does a deeper group-2 freeze (E046-style) stay on the dial's line, or does it hit a cliff like E037?
